questions.text: A. Each file stored on any computing device, in every directory contains information describing such files. List and define (where appropriate) any 6 file descriptors. (3 marks)

B. A certain computing device, for personal use, was designed to run several applications, some of which are over 1GB in size. This device was labelled as Core i7, with 32GB RAM and a 1TB hard disk, among other specifications. Having studied operating systems, you know that this computing device needs an Operating System to function properly.
i. Describe (with any suitable diagram) the arrangement of the processor(s) for this computing device. (6 marks)

B. A certain computing device, for personal use, was designed to run several applications, some of which are over 1GB in size. This device was labelled as Core i7, with 32GB RAM and a 1TB hard disk, among other specifications. Having studied operating systems, you know that this computing device needs an Operating System to function properly.
ii. Briefly describe the Memory allocation scheme you think the operating system should employ. (4 marks)

D. What is a lockword? (2 marks)

A. Jobs A, B, C, and D have some of their pages already resident in memory that uses demand paged memory allocation scheme. Job C then requests that another page of its job be loaded into the memory. Write an algorithm that might be used to load any Job's page into the memory, bearing in mind that it is possible for all the page frames to be occupied. (4 marks)
C. Define the following terms: i. Thrashing (2 marks) ii. Page fault (1 mark) iii. Page swapping (2 marks)

B. To prevent the processor from spending more time doing overhead than executing jobs, the operating system must continuously monitor the system and feed this information to the Job Scheduler via a mechanism. What is this mechanism called and how does it function? (4 marks)

D. There are three methods to enforce mutual exclusion in a multiprocessing environment. These three methods can be classified into hardware methods and software methods.
i. Describe the hardware methods and state the main advantage one has over the other. (5 marks)
ii. Describe the software method. (2 marks)

The Management of Charles University decided for safety purposes, that students should no longer cook in their rooms. They have provided kitchenettes on all the floors in the hostels where students must cook. Each kitchenette is equipped with 3 pots, 2 hotplates, 2 knives, 1 chop board, 2 frying pans, a dustbin and 5 taps for water; these are not to be taken away from the kitchenette. Students are allowed to bring any other item they need to cook except the provided items. Once a student takes any of the provided items she is not to release it until she is done using it even if she is waiting for other items. In addition to that, you cannot start cooking until you have all you need. You can only cook on your floor. In addition to that, students are not allowed to share any of the provided items. After having lectures all day, Eunice, Affiong, Jane, Busayo and Fatima who reside on the same floor, decided to cook their dinner. Luckily for them, the kitchenette was empty.

Eunice wants to make concoction Spaghetti, so she quickly grabs a pot and starts to prepare her ingredients. Eunice needs a hotplate to complete her cooking. Affiong, who wants to make jollof rice also picks a pot to start her food preparation. She is yet to get a hotplate. Jane wants to make rice and stew in two separate pots. Jane grabs a pot for her rice and puts it on a hotplate. She still needs a knife to start chopping onion and tomatoes and a hotplate to make her stew. Busayo wants to make dodo and fried eggs so she takes a knife to start slicing her plantain. She would need a hotplate, frying pan and chop board to complete her cooking. Fatima is eating light; she takes a chop board, puts all her vegetables for making salad on it and needs a knife to start chopping.

At this point, the floor manager, Abigail enters the kitchenette amidst all the commotion and thinks that these ladies will not be able to finish cooking their meals.

A. With respect to deadlocks, what would you term the underlined phrase. Define the condition that is depicted by the underlined phrase. (3 marks) [The underlining is not visible in the copy used.]
B. Using deadlock models, draw a directed graph depicting the current situation of the kitchenette to assist Abigail know its current state. Please state your assumptions. (10 marks)
C. With respect to the knives alone, define the situation between Jane and Fatima. (2 marks)
D. If Abigail decides to resolve the commotion, what steps will she take to make it worse? (2 marks)
E. Is it possible for Abigail to assist these ladies to finish cooking their meals in peace? If so, list the steps Abigail should take and the results of each step. (3 marks)

A. A young Computer Scientist has heard about OS interrupts and he's been wondering what they are or why they're even needed. He's wondering if the computer would do just as well without interrupts as with interrupts. In concise terms and with the aid of a diagram, help him understand the concept of OS interrupts, the need for them and some various classes of interrupts. (10 marks)
B. If you are to design a multi-user real-time system using the concept of concurrent processing, which configuration would you implement and why? (10 marks)
